title: The Gap in Her Story
warm:
The gap in her story found her anyway—Nolan Greer standing in [player_name]'s apartment across the hall with the unnamed night already mapped in his eyes. Early thirties, she/her, soft alibi with one withheld hour she had worn like underwear under cover. Crownspire's glass hush pressed the door. Detective Imani Brooks's homicide climb lived in every unfinished sentence. Vivienne's four fates stayed open on purpose: willing leave, paid vanish, dead, staging.

"You unlocked my drawer," Nolan said. Mid-forties, finance and tech holding, brutal charm raw without cufflink polish tonight. "You kept one night unnamed. Black car too long at the curb. Bag by a door. Perfume capped mid-exit. I found the gap because soft alibi is still a story, and stories leave holes money can feel."

[player_name] did not invent a corpse. She had only refused to inventory what she saw—the night Vivienne's cadence might have tipped from monthly toward gone, the night that might still be travel or staging or something colder. Soft meant pliable; withheld meant she still owned one private truth. Now Nolan owned the knowledge that she had withheld it.

Wine glass rings on her own marble looked like exhibits. Elevator chime trembled in the shared shaft. Somewhere below, Rhea Quinn's slate still carried thinning marks; Marcus Pell would have preferred she invent nothing. Across twelve steps, Nolan's penthouse waited with silent-partner paper and unused perfume she should not know.

"You can speak the night-truth aloud to me," Nolan said, voice low, "read what you saw into bed and consequence. Or you can burn it—mercy or cowardice, Layer 8 will name which. Neither settles Vivienne. Both spend the soft we built."

Hope and dread shared the hallway. Brooks's badge had stopped sounding like missing-persons alone. Soft alibi had fingerprints and a gap; the gap had become a door. [player_name] felt the unnamed hour rearrange itself around her throat like expensive silk she had not agreed to own.

Choice verbs waited: night-truth spoken into intimacy and pressure, or night-truth burned before Brooks could subpoena the private throb. Crownspire held its hush. Cufflink almost. Perfume ghost from across the hall. City light as accusation through floor-to-ceiling glass. She understood that being found had already changed which soft she could still claim.
hot:
Gap heat meant Nolan Greer already inside [player_name]'s apartment across the hall, mid-forties body too close, early thirties soft alibi throbbing around the unnamed night he had mapped anyway. Soft cover had a pulse. Rain-money cologne. Vivienne's unused perfume as third heat ghosting from his side of the corridor. Brooks's colder file vibrated through Crownspire glass into her bloodstream without a corpse to make her nipples tight under silk.

"You kept the car, the bag, the perfume capped mid-exit from me," he murmured, mouth almost on the hinge of her jaw. Cufflink metal kissed her wrist when he caught her hand. "I found the gap. Soft alibi still leaves you wet for consequence. Choose—speak the night-truth into bed with me, or burn it while your cunt still aches around what you saw."

Crime stayed plot; sex stayed intimacy-forward, never gore. Heat was trust versus complicity wearing a body. Four fates open. No settled corpse. [player_name]'s thighs tightened as his thumb counted ribs. Mid-want ending first—climax belonging to the verb she spent.

She arched once, fine and furious. "If I speak it," she whispered, palm flat on his chest, "I become co-author of the hour I hid." A beat. "If I burn it, I wear mercy or cowardice with a private throb Brooks doesn't inventory yet."

Nolan's mouth hovered. Elevator chime trembled through her teeth. Wine-ringed marble. Black car memory curb-idle like a held breath. She trembled choosing, unfinished on purpose, romance locked on Nolan Greer alone while Vivienne stayed contested and homicide interest rose without naming a body.

Body through-line: waist, mouth, thighs, unfinished pulse. Soft alibi heat ended on the hook of choice because climax belonged to night-truth spoken or burned.
